size_pct_nav: Approximately US$1bn initial disclosed short notional, roughly 9% of contemporary US$11bn AUM; not an authenticated trade-date NAV or premium-at-risk weight.

drivers.driver: Alleged compensation primarily rewarded recruitment rather than genuine outside retail demand.
drivers.source: https://www.10xebitda.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/11/Pershing-Square-Herbalife-Presentation-Dec-2012.pdf (2012-12-20, after cutoff; original presentation recovered in this pass)

drivers.driver: Questioned distributor success claims, retail-sales measurement and losses borne by lower-level participants.
drivers.quote: In a pyramid scheme, the money at the top is made from the losses of people at the bottom of the pyramid

drivers.driver: Expected regulatory shutdown or collapse to destroy equity value; this was Pershing's allegation, not an adjudicated fact.
drivers.quote: HLF is an illegal pyramid scheme that will collapse or otherwise be shut down by regulators.

drivers.driver: Expected economic deterioration to validate the thesis, but later acknowledged fundamental analysis alone was insufficient for a viable short.
drivers.quote: While we believe that deteriorating business fundamentals and a high valuation are a good recipe for an attractive short sale, technical factors are a critically important additional consideration.

entry_valuation_stated: Initial weighted-average short-sale price and first execution date unverified. US$42.50 is the December 18 market close, not an asserted execution price. Zero-price target depended on an adverse regulatory/business outcome, not conventional multiple compression.
outcome_note: FTC July 15, 2016 settlement required major US compensation/business restructuring and US$200m consumer redress, but did not shut Herbalife down or constitute a court finding of an illegal pyramid. The short lost money; approximate US$1bn lifetime-loss reporting is not independently reconstructed audited P&L. Open short was converted to puts in 2017 to cap risk; position exited by February 2018. The 2017 letter says reduced free float, buybacks and technical factors made the short increasingly risky. Good selected fundamental/regulatory observations did not ensure successful security selection or timing. Later process moved away from public single-name short campaigns; no claim that this was the only cause.
pack_quality_notes: Eight documents of pre-December19 information. Financials and October29 guidance, explicit external-retail measurement gap, company response, three peers, buyback funding, 13F and current AUM. Later original pitch used only in key. Null first-action date preserves actual uncertainty. No fabricated borrow fee, locate, short interest, consensus estimate, original NAV weight or regulatory decision. 13F call rows carefully separated from common shares; historical HLF split basis corrected.
